# Sidebar

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

navigation and disclosure · tier 2 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For the links of an app, in a rail beside the page that collapses to a column of icons.
Every link is in the HTML the server sends; only the rail and its toggle run in the browser.

```ts
import { Icon, SidebarBody, SidebarGroup, SidebarHeader, SidebarLink, SidebarRoot } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<div className="flex h-dvh">
  <SidebarRoot>
    <SidebarHeader>Workspace</SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarBody>
      <SidebarGroup label="Getting started">
        <SidebarLink href="/docs/install" icon={<Icon name="download-simple" />} current>Install</SidebarLink>
        <SidebarLink href="/docs/theming" icon={<Icon name="palette" />}>Theming</SidebarLink>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarBody>
  </SidebarRoot>
  <main className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto">Your page</main>
</div>
```

- **Parts.** Six flat names and no bare `Sidebar`. `SidebarRoot` and `SidebarTrigger` run in
  the browser; `SidebarHeader`, `SidebarBody`, `SidebarGroup` and `SidebarLink` are server
  HTML. `SidebarHeader` draws the toggle itself.
- **Height.** Give the parent of the rail a height, such as `h-dvh`. A long list then
  scrolls inside `SidebarBody`, and the page does not.
- **Beside the page.** In a flex row the rail keeps its 220 px, or 60 collapsed. Give the
  column beside it `min-w-0 flex-1`.
- **Collapsed from the start.** `defaultOpen={false}`. The server sends it collapsed, so
  nothing moves when the page hydrates.
- **A link.** Pass `href`, or `render={<Link href="/docs" />}` in Next.js. Every other prop
  goes to the link, not to the `<li>` around it.
- **The current page.** `current` on one link sets `aria-current="page"` and draws the
  row filled, bold and with a bar at its start.
- **Give every link an `icon`** when the rail can collapse. Collapsed, the icon is all that
  is drawn: a link without one is an empty row, still a tab stop and still named.
- **Collapsed, nothing loses its name.** The title, the label of a group and the label of
  a link are hidden, and a screen reader still reads them.
- **A group.** `label` names its list. With no label it is a plain list.
- **Your own state.** `open` with `onOpenChange` needs a `'use client'` file: see
  `dummy/controlled.tsx`. A button outside the rail can then toggle it.
- **Another width.** `className="data-open:w-72"` on `SidebarRoot`. The collapsed width
  stays.
- **On a phone** an expanded rail takes 220 of 320 px. Start it collapsed there, or hide
  it: the drawer form is not built yet.
- **A long label** ends in an ellipsis at the width of the rail, and is cut at 100
  characters.
- **Arabic.** Under `dir="rtl"` the rail's line is on its left and the toggle on its right,
  with its icon mirrored. `TopClassProvider` with `locale="ar"` names both in Arabic.
- **Keyboard.** Tab goes to the toggle, then to each link. Enter or Space presses the
  toggle.
- **Scrollbar.** Collapsed, the scrollbar of a long list is not drawn. The wheel, a finger
  and the keys still scroll it.

### What each part takes

| Part | Prop | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `SidebarRoot` | `defaultOpen`, `open`, `onOpenChange` | The state, its own or yours. |
| `SidebarRoot` | `aria-label` | Another name than "Sidebar", for a page with two rails. |
| `SidebarTrigger` | `onClick` | Runs first. `event.preventDefault()` stops the toggle. |
| `SidebarHeader` | children | The title beside the toggle. |
| `SidebarBody` | children | The groups. It is the part that scrolls. |
| `SidebarGroup` | `label` | The heading of the group, which names its list. |
| `SidebarLink` | `href` or `render` | Where the row goes. One of the two is required. |
| `SidebarLink` | children or `aria-label` | The name of the row. An `href` link needs one; a `render` element may carry its own text. |
| `SidebarLink` | `icon`, `current` | The icon, the current page. |

### Not built

`width` as a prop (pass `data-open:w-72`), remembering the state between visits, a width
animation, a tooltip on a collapsed link (a mouse user sees the icon alone), the mobile
overlay (the AdaptiveSidebar connector), nested groups, a letter in place of a missing
icon, and a custom scrollbar.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  SidebarRoot,
  SidebarTrigger,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarBody,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarLink,
  SidebarSkeleton,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `children` or `render` on `SidebarLink`, `href` or `render` on `SidebarLink`, `aria-label` or `children` or `href` or `render` on `SidebarLink`. Every other prop below is optional.

### SidebarRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | A SidebarHeader, then a SidebarBody holding the groups and their links. |
| `defaultOpen` | no | `boolean` | `true` | SidebarRoot: whether the rail starts expanded. false starts it as a column of icons, in the server HTML too. |
| `onOpenChange` | no | `((open: boolean) => void)` | - | Called with the state the trigger asks for, once a press. A function: pass it from a client file. |
| `open` | no | `boolean` | - | SidebarRoot: the state, held by the caller. Pair it with onOpenChange, in a client file. |

### SidebarTrigger

This part takes no design props of its own.

### SidebarHeader

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The title beside the trigger. It is hidden, and still read out, while the rail is collapsed. |

### SidebarBody

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The groups. A list longer than the rail scrolls here, under the header. |

### SidebarGroup

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The SidebarLink rows of the group. |
| `label` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The heading of the group, which names its list. Hidden, and still read out, while the rail is collapsed. |

### SidebarLink

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `children` or `render` | `string` | - |  |
| `children` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `render` | `ReactNode` | - | The label. It ends in an ellipsis when the rail is too narrow, and is cut at 100 characters. |
| `href` | **yes**, or `render` | `string` | - | Where the row goes. |
| `render` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `children` or `href` | `ReactElement` | - | The link as another element, such as `render={<Link href="/docs" />}`, which carries its own href. |
| `current` | no | `boolean` | `false` | SidebarLink: the page being read. It sets aria-current="page" and draws the row filled, bold and marked. |
| `icon` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Drawn before the label, and all that is drawn while the rail is collapsed. Decorative: the label names the row. |

### SidebarSkeleton

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | no | `boolean` | `true` | SidebarSkeleton: whether the rail it stands in for is expanded. Pass what its defaultOpen or open will be. |
| `links` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 200 | `4` | SidebarSkeleton: how many link rows the placeholder holds, clamped to 1 and 200. |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
